requirements.requirement: Convert each decodable manifest-listed input into normalized/ under the matching filename as valid UTF-8 with LF line endings, preserving accented characters, empty records, and each input's final-newline state.
requirements.summary: western.txt and utf8.txt were published under matching names. Exact byte-level transformation checks confirmed valid UTF-8, zero CR bytes, preserved accented characters, one empty western.txt record, and respective final bytes 0a and 64; all checks also passed after restart.

requirements.requirement: Report undecodable input without character replacement or partial publication.
requirements.summary: invalid.txt produced an explicit illegal UTF-8 sequence report at position 15. No normalized/invalid.txt or staging artifact was published, both before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep all incoming source files intact.
requirements.summary: All three incoming files retained the exact SHA-256 hashes recorded in the preparation baseline, both before and after the node restart.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 16.04.7 LTS and kernel 4.4.0-210-generic remained unchanged through execution and restart. Conversion used the platform's installed iconv and Perl utilities, and the resulting files passed direct validation.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for node1: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot ID, running system state, and recovered source/output integrity were directly observed and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot snapshots.
limitations: Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was identified. The failed early attempts did not create files because normalized/ was absent or unwritable; creating normalized/ and publishing the two outputs was necessary task work. Temporary conversion files were removed, no staging artifacts remained, and the required restart left no failed services, new listeners, package damage, or abnormal temporary residue. The boot-ID change and recovered data were fully demonstrated.
